mission: Prepare the real-user zero-handholding usability test (versioned observation protocol + confusion-event instrumentation) and audit the mobile UX copy/flows against it on simulator-free surfaces, fixing concrete clarity defects with tests.
method: Read docs/STATUS_BOARD.md and docs/HANDOFF_V4_DRAFT.md, then read the actual mobile flow surfaces (AnalyzeScreen, CaptureGuidancePanel, UncertaintyNote, TechniqueIntentPicker, tryAgainHandoff, runCaptureAnalysis, capture.ts) before writing any protocol claims.

Wrote a versioned protocol (zero-handholding-usability-v1) with tasks T1-T9 covering: open Stroke Analysis, choose technique/Auto Detect, place the phone, tap the starting location, understand readiness, walk out, swing, receive a Result, understand uncertainty, Try Again.

Built a shared instrumentation contract (apps/mobile/src/analysis/usabilityTelemetry.ts): a 13-step funnel recorder, frozen v1 confusion thresholds, deterministic pure derivation of machine confusion events, and a separate human observer-coded confusion vocabulary. Telemetry is observational only - it never gates or alters capture, readiness, or scoring.

Wired the funnel into AnalyzeScreen (open, intent selection, camera open, readiness states, ready, stroke captured, capture saved, analysis started, honest outcome shown, result opened, errors, abandonment, try-again rearm), reusing existing targetLock evidence for the start-location step rather than inventing new claims.

Audited copy against the protocol and fixed concrete defects with tests: added the previously missing explicit starting-location walkthrough step ('Tap where you will start... walk out to it'), humanized snake_case envelope dimension names in the quality-blocked reason, renamed a misleading 'locked' funnel detail to 'start_tapped' when no lock telemetry exists, and pinned readiness-copy coverage of every CameraReadinessState.

Added __tests__/usabilityTelemetry.test.ts (recorder, thresholds, confusion derivation, funnel summaries) and __tests__/zeroHandholdingCopyAudit.test.ts (readiness copy coverage/actionability, walkthrough steps, captureSavedDetail honesty against assertCapturedClip-validated clips).
deliverables: docs/USABILITY_ZERO_HANDHOLDING.md (protocol zero-handholding-usability-v1; zero sessions run - no user data exists or was fabricated)
apps/mobile/src/screens/AnalyzeScreen.tsx (funnel wiring, exported ANALYZE_STEPS with new starting-location step, exported READINESS_COPY typed over CameraReadinessState, captureSavedDetail)
apps/mobile/src/analysis/runCaptureAnalysis.ts (human-readable dimension names in the honest quality-blocked reason)

gates.root: pnpm typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm format:check all pass on this branch
gates.mobile: npx tsc --noEmit passes; npm test passes (42 suites, 421 tests)
gates.mobileLintNote: apps/mobile's own `npm run lint` crashes on a preexisting eslint 8/9 version clash (fails on App.tsx before any of this branch's files); root `pnpm lint` covers the touched TS/TSX and passes.

irreducibly_external: Running the protocol itself: fresh real users on a physical iPhone (GATE B surface). No sessions have been run; funnel counts and confusion events in this branch are structure only, with zero recorded data.

Whether fresh users actually comprehend the copy (starting-location tap, readiness states, abstention explanations, withheld-score uncertainty) - only live think-aloud sessions can answer; the protocol lists these as live-user-only questions.
Native camera/readiness behavior on device (Apple Vision pose, target lock timing) - Mac/iPhone toolchain unavailable on Linux; nothing was fabricated.

GATE A remains fully external: no coach evidence exists; technique score, fault diagnosis, and drill recommendation stay BLOCKED_ON_VALIDATION. Usability results can never substitute for coach validation.
Held-out cases wm-dink-01 and afn-vic-rally1 were not touched.
verdict: READY_FOR_LIVE_SESSIONS: the zero-handholding usability test is fully specified and instrumented, and the auditable copy defects found are fixed with tests. Only real users on a real device can produce the usability evidence itself.
